request.summary: Prove that a portable Wayfinding Studio runtime artifact can power a polished interactive Wallboard custom app in both 2D and 3D.
request.audience: Visitors using a landscape touch display at a modern campus.
request.primaryGoal: Let a visitor select a destination and inspect a reviewed route while rotating, panning, and zooming the same semantic map in 3D.

assumptions: The Northline campus data is synthetic and license-safe.
The bundled runtime JSON represents the exact portable contract emitted by Wayfinding Studio.
The primary surfaces are Full HD and 1366x768 landscape touch displays.

surfaceStrategy.rationale: The map and touch directory form a deliberate landscape kiosk composition.

ownership.rationale: Reviewed geometry, graph topology, labels, and presentation travel together as one Studio runtime artifact.
Operators control kiosk identity and safe presentation choices without changing reviewed geometry.
Selection and camera movement belong to the active visitor session.

views.purpose: Rotate, pan, zoom, select extruded spaces, and inspect the route.
Use the same artifact as a flat accessible fallback.

inputs.action: Rotate, pan, zoom, and select destinations.
Select a destination or reset the view.

session.expectation: Reset clears destination selection and restores the authored 3D camera.

rendering.rationale: The map owns all available space beside a fixed, readable directory.

motion.rationale: The current position pulses while visitor camera movement remains direct and touch-controlled.

branding.provenance: Northline is a fictional campus identity controlled through safe operator settings.

settings.purpose: Allows visitors to switch between the two renderers.
Controls current-position pulse without changing direct visitor camera control.
Selects the coordinated Light, Dark, or Custom palette.

dynamicText.fallback: Keep the complete name where space permits and use one-line ellipsis only after the readable floor.
dynamicText.rationale: The kiosk identity must stay readable without changing header height.

dynamicText.fallback: Wrap names to two lines and scroll the directory instead of shrinking below the touch-readable floor.

states.expectation: The nonblank 3D map, complete directory, and authored camera fill the Full-HD kiosk.
The same interaction remains readable at 1366x768.
The 2D renderer uses the same zones, labels, origin, and graph route.
The coordinated dark interface keeps the 3D scene and directory legible.

behaviors.expectation: The packaged custom app renders nonblank WebGL from the Studio artifact.
Destination selection drives the same graph route in 3D and 2D.
Reset clears selection and restores the authored camera without recreating the app.

visualDirection.summary: A warm architectural model rather than a dashboard: clean extruded campus spaces, persistent billboard labels, and one compact directory.
signatureChoices: The semantic floor model is the full-bleed primary object rather than a card.
Each destination has a distinct architectural color and Studio-authored height.
avoid: Decorative perspective that blocks route inspection

visualReview.intent: A convincing real custom-app proof that Studio output can become a touch-controlled spatial wayfinding product.
focus: Verify the WebGL canvas is nonblank and correctly framed.
Verify labels float above their matching extrusions without clipping.
Verify route and selection remain obvious in both 2D and 3D.
Verify no control or directory text overlaps at either accepted surface.
